summary: Mapped 4 concrete archive/vault hand-rolled write sites in the declared file_scope (2 in task.md, 1 in todo.md, 1 in skill-todo/SKILL.md) plus 3 prose-only sites. Found one real design fork: the vault archive-reinit is a fresh-file create, not a transform, so a plain --state-file flag cannot cover it alone -- needs an --init/no-input mode or an explicit scope-acquire/scope-release bracket. Flagged task-lock.md's residual-surface note as stale (needs correcting regardless), and named several out-of-file_scope sites (archive-task.sh, vault-operation.sh -- which already hand-rolls a live specs/state.json write with zero mutex --, jq-escaping-workarounds.md examples, review.md's specs/reviews/state.json, and the large pre-existing extension-domain debt) that will keep the verification bar's literal repo-wide-zero-hits grep from passing unless explicitly scoped or reported.
decisions_made: Recommend a single specs/.scope-lock mutex for all --state-file targets, not per-file locks, to avoid an ABBA deadlock between concurrent recover/abandon-style interleaved operations.
Recommend --regen-todo be refused as a usage error when combined with a non-default --state-file.

Recommend the vault archive-reinit site be resolved via either a state-write.sh --init/no-input mode or an explicit scope-acquire/scope-release bracket around the existing jq -n write, since it is a fresh-create with no existing file to transform.
